$comment: GENERATED by `cargo run -p deck-space --features schema --bin deck-schema` from deck-space's SceneDocument (scene_document.rs) – do not edit.

Arrange.description: A spawn zone's arrangement: its kind and the spacing between members.

spacing.description: metres between neighbours (a set's spot is a point: the spacing says how wide the zone grows)

ArrangeKind.description: The arrangements of a first version (scene_resolve.rs `arrange`): more (a stack, a crowd) when a use needs one.

oneOf.description: side by side across the spot, centred on it (a choir on the altar, items on a table)
around the spot, the first in its middle, the next on a widening ring (crows on a beam's end, a crowd's core)

Fill.description:
The filter of a placeholder (SCENES.md §9.2): the address book's typeahead question, stored. Within a fact any value
admits; every fact given must hold (owner 2026-11-12, §9.7 Q5).

kind.description:
the address book's kinds that may fill it (required): a holder's of `character`, `persona`, `look`, `item`; a
location's `location`

parent.description: only entries below this reference (`character:catpope`: her personas and looks)

ref.description: a hand-picked list of references (`character:catpope`, `item:incense`); none = any of the kinds

Fillers.description: One filler or several (a spawn zone's members).

Holder.description: One place on the stage (SCENE-PACKAGE §2, SCENES.md §9.3).

arrange.description: a spawn zone's arrangement of its members within the spot (required with `take: many`)

enter.description: `start` (the default): on stage when the scene starts; `join`: waits for the story (`joinScene`, SCENES.md §9.4)

id.description:
its name in the document and in a use's `with` (`left`, `who`); not an address – a filled holder's address is its
filler's place (`scene:stage/character:catpope/…`), an empty one has none

max.description: a spawn zone's limit; none = any number

preview.description: fillers for the editor and the browser (a spawn zone may preview several)

ref.description: an authored filler (`character:catpope`, `item:incense`) – or `fill`, never both

rig.description: the rig its filler plays; none = the filler's own (`character:catpope` → `rig:character.catpope`)

spot.description: the spot of the set where it stands and enters (`spot_left`); none = the scene's spot

take.description: `one` filler (the default) or `many`: a spawn zone (owner 2026-11-12 [scenes]) – a placeholder only

values.description:
values and preset choices only (SCENE-PACKAGE §2), by address: `"voice:voice.index": 4.0`,
`"voice:@preset": "cathedral_voice.bright"`

HolderValue.description: A holder's value: a parameter's number, or a track's preset choice.

map.description:
an audio link's channel map (plan 2.6, #318): `[source, target]` pairs counted from 1 – `[[1, 3], [2, 4]]` lands a
stereo source on channels 3 and 4 (a send's offset); one source may go to several targets, several sources into one
target sum. Empty = channel n to channel n. `scale` on an audio link is the send level.

LocationPlaceholder.description: A location no scene names yet: what may fill it.

id.description: its name in a use's `with` (`where`, `home`); not an address

preview.description: a filler for the editor and the browser

anyOf.description: filled by a use (`with.<id>`): authored, or by context (a location's default scene: the location)

LocationSlot.description: The scene's location: a reference, or a placeholder.

RigPin.description: A rig by reference and the version it was wired against (SCENE-PACKAGE §2).

version.description:
the version it was wired against: the rig's `version` as scene-content serves it (16 hex of its data's SHA-256 –
the catalog keeps no version number); none = the current one

SceneTransition.description: What a switch does to the outputs (the lamps) between two scenes (#264).

oneOf.description: hold the last values, then crossfade to the new scene's over `transition_secs`; channels it doesn't drive fade to 0
the new scene takes over at once; channels it doesn't drive go to 0
the lamps go dark first (the outputs stop and start again), like a stop

audio_buffer.description:
the audio device's buffer in frames (#208, deck-native's audio/backend.rs): a heavy scene may ask for more;
`--audio-buffer` and deck.toml's `audio_buffer` (the machine's) win over it. None = the device's default

render_scale.description: the render size relative to the window (0.25–1); a software adapter halves it by itself

transition.description:
how the stage hands over TO this scene on a switch (F5, #264): the DMX / MIDI outputs of the scene that was playing
fade into this one's (`fade`, the default), snap (`cut`) or go dark first (`blackout`); a stop is always dark

transition_secs.description: the hand-over's length in s (`fade`); the same time base as the picture's fade in (deck-native switcher.rs `FADE_IN`)

Take.description: How many fillers a holder takes.

oneOf.description: a spawn zone: several fillers of what its `fill` allows, arranged by code

description: One `scene:<id>` document as the API stores it.

format.description: the document's format: 2 (location, holders, spawn zones; #489)

holder.description: the places on its stage, in the order a story's `joinScene` tries them (SCENES.md §9.4)

id.description: the key's id: `nave` for `scene:nave` – platform-wide, no toon in it (a scene can serve several toons and shows)

location.description: where it plays: `location:<id>`, or a placeholder a use fills; none = the `space` node's own `set` (or no set)

node.description: the scene's own nodes (the space, mixers); the holders' rigs are flattened in by the resolve step

toons.description: the toons whose address books list it; empty = reachable by its id only (a template: listed in every book, 2·2)

version.description: the number the server stamps on every change (as a show's); absent until the first save
